messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] sex specific QTL analysis
parts:
From what I can see, what you need to do is the following:

sex <- pull.pheno(q, "sex")
male <- subset(q, ind=(sex==1))
ac.male <- ac[sex==1,]
out.m <- scanone(male, addcovar=ac.male)

A few comments on your code:

> > out.m <- scanone(subset(q, ind = sex==1),addcovar=ac[sex==1,])
> Error in subset.cross(q, ind = sex == 1) :
> Must retain at least one individual.

The 'sex' vector must not be the same as pull.pheno(q, sex).

> > out.m <- scanone(subset(male, ind = sex==1),addcovar=ac[sex==1,])
> Error in subset.cross(male, ind = sex == 1) :
> ind argument has wrong length (283; should be 138)

Since you'd already subseted by sex to create the 'male' dataset, you don't want to do it again here.

One last point: use caution in comparing the results of the separate analyses of males and females. Evidence for a QTL in one sex and not the other doesn't mean that it is a sex-specific QTL. I avoid saying "sex-specific QTL" as much as possible, but instead focus on whether there is a sex-difference in the effect of the QTL (in other words, is there a QTL-by-sex interaction?). For that, you need to compare the model with sex as an interactive covariate to the model with sex as just an additive covariate.

karl
